idh.reasoning: The metadata favors IDH-wildtype because the lesion pattern is multifocal with satellites and very extensive edema relative to the small tumor core, with a recorded necrotic/non-enhancing core and mild enhancement; this constellation is more typical of an aggressive adult diffuse glioma than a conventional IDH-mutant lower-grade tumor. Absence of a T2-FLAIR mismatch also does not provide the classic imaging support for IDH-mutant astrocytoma. Evidence against IDH-wildtype includes the frontal/cortical distribution, absent deep white matter invasion, absent ependymal invasion, and only mild/tiny enhancement, which can be seen in IDH-mutant tumors. On balance, the multifocal satellite pattern and disproportionate edema support IDH-wildtype.

The main uncertainty is that frontal cortical location supports an oligodendroglioma-spectrum possibility, while multifocal satellites and disproportionate edema support an aggressive non-codeleted, IDH-wildtype pattern.

who_grade.reasoning: For grade considered independently, the presence of necrotic/non-enhancing core, thick enhancing margin, multifocal disease with satellites, and very extensive edema all favor CNS WHO grade 4 over grades 2 or 3. Overall, necrosis together with multifocal satellites and marked edema most strongly supports grade 4.
